title: Try/Catch Async Errors Check
description: Handle Promise rejections with try/catch and toResult.

questions.explanation: `await` on a rejection throws inside the async function, so `try/catch` logs `caught boom`.

questions.prompt: If an `async` function throws (or rejects), what happens to its returned Promise?
questions.explanation: Throwing or rejecting inside `async` rejects the Promise that the function returned.

questions.prompt: What does a successful `toResult(promise)` typically return?
questions.explanation: The `toResult` pattern normalizes success into `{ ok: true, value }` so callers can branch without `try/catch`.

questions.prompt: Why use `toResult` instead of only relying on uncaught rejections?

options.text: It makes Promises run on multiple threads
Callers can branch on `{ ok, value }` vs `{ ok: false, error }` without crashing
It converts sync errors into `setTimeout` callbacks

questions.explanation: `toResult` turns fulfillment/rejection into a plain result object so callers can handle both paths explicitly.
